title: Charlie Barnet's offer, Willard Alexander and Lester's praise of Billie Holiday
summary: Jones describes Barnet's plan for Basie, Willard Alexander's visit to the Reno Club, and Lester telling him about Billie Holiday before Hammond.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: What did Charlie Barnet's letter say?

He wanted to have Basie like a Lester Lanin or like a Meyer Davis. He was going to sponsor the band. They had heard the band's broadcast from Chicago. Then he went back and he brought Willard Alexander into the Reno Club and Willard sat on a stool and he saw the band with his mouth wide open for half an hour.
John Hammond had been with Billie Holiday before this?

Oh sure, he had started with Billie Holiday. He was out here on the East Coast; we don't know nothing about this, because like I said, Lester Young was telling me after he came back from Minneapolis and he said, 'Lady J, here's a girl I want you to hear her sing.' I said, 'Lester, I don't care nothing about no singers.' He said, 'But you should hear her sing. She can sing!' See, Lester knew about Billie Holiday before any of us knew, because he came in with Fletcher Henderson in 1933 and he found out what this poor singer - but Lester had been hanging out with singers. He said, 'This girl can sing! She has a distinctive style.' I said, 'There ain't no broad can sing, after Genevieve Stearns, Arcola Cole, and Clara Campbell, there ain't no girl can sing.' Then by that time Ella Fitzgerald come up and you knew about Ella, that did the thing with Benny Goodman. Ella Fitzgerald, you remember.
She was with Chick Webb and she just went

down and made a recording with Benny. But I said, "Lester, I don't know nothing about that." Then here come John Hammond. But John had seen Lester when he came in with Fletcher Henderson, up to Clarks Monroe's Uptown House. At that time, that was the only place.
He must have played in New York with Fletcher Henderson before you played in New York with Basie.

Of course. I was sitting there, I didn't know about this guy. So John came in and I looked at him and said, "John, you don't impress me." And we went through a personal thing. I said, "You don't want to see me; you want to see Basie." But he didn't know where Basie was. I did, so I got Basie for him. Then John left and then when he came back with Willard Alexander, because Willard was building the Benny Goodman band with Gene Krupa and Lionel Hampton.
